# Survey of Consumer Finances: dataset risk assessment

**Assessment date: October 9, 2026**  
**Primary publisher:** Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System  
**Primary location:** [Federal Reserve SCF release site](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm)

## Overall finding

**I found no evidence that the SCF has been terminated, that historical survey waves have been withdrawn, or that its next publication has missed its announced schedule.** The 2025 survey has active collection approval through August 2027, and its summary results are expected in late 2026.

The principal concerns are **institutional capacity and weak survey-specific statutory protection**:

- The Federal Reserve has announced approximately **10% staffing reductions over several years**, restricted hiring, and reduced some planned technology spending.
- Political efforts to remove Federal Reserve governors create leadership uncertainty.
- The SCF supports statutory Federal Reserve responsibilities, but the cited statutes do **not expressly require this particular survey, its questionnaire, its triennial frequency, or public microdata publication**.

The ratings below distinguish **observed changes** from **potential risks**. “No Known Issue” is not a guarantee of continued availability. This assessment reviewed release listings and documentation; it is **not a complete download-and-checksum audit of every historical file**.

---

## 1. Historical Data Availability

### Selected level: **No Known Issue**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | Not supported. Historical survey resources remain publicly listed. |
| **High Risk** | No evidence found that previously available survey-wave files have been removed. |
| **Moderate Risk** | No evidence found of a recent withdrawal of previously public historical variables. Longstanding confidentiality exclusions are not evidence of a new removal. |
| **No Known Issue** | The Board maintains previous-wave pages, public data listings, weights, and documentation extending back decades. |

### Supporting evidence

- The Board’s [Previous Surveys page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scf-previous-surveys.htm) links to the 1983–2019 surveys, historical panels, pension-provider studies, and 1962–1963 predecessor studies.
- The [2019 release page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scf_2019.htm) continues to list full public microdata in SAS, Stata, and ASCII; replicate weights; summary extracts; and documentation.
- The [1983 release page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scf_1983.htm) still lists public data and extensive technical documentation.
- The central release site provides historical tables covering **1989–2022**.

**Important qualification:** the files are not immutable. The Board updates extracts, inflation adjustments, and corrections, with dated listings and change documentation. For example, the 2019 page lists summary extracts updated in April 2024. Such documented revisions are different from destructive alteration or withdrawal.

**Why this rating:** there is no identified historical-access loss. I interpret “no known alterations” in this risk rubric as no known harmful or unexplained alterations—not an assertion that the dataset has never received a legitimate correction.

**Confidence:** Moderate; historical listings are extensive, but every binary file and historical vintage was not independently validated.

---

## 2. Future Data Availability

### Selected level: **No Known Issue**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | Not supported. The Board announced the 2025 collection, and NORC confirms interviewing began. |
| **High Risk** | No skipped cycle, statutory deadline violation, or approval lapse exceeding one year was identified. |
| **Moderate Risk** | No announced publication delay or expired ICR was identified. |
| **No Known Issue** | Collection approval is active, and the announced late-2026 publication window has not clearly been missed. |

### Supporting evidence

- The Board’s [February 28, 2025 announcement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/other20250228a.htm) states that **summary results will be published in late 2026**.
- [NORC’s participant page](https://www.norc.org/contact/study-participants/scf.html) confirms that interviewing began in March 2025.
- The Board’s [participant information page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/scf/scf.htm) identifies OMB control number **7100-0287**, expiring **August 31, 2027**.
- The [July 31, 2024 Federal Register notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/07/31/2024-16768/agency-information-collection-activities-announcement-of-board-approval-under-delegated-authority) extended FR 3059 for three years **without revision**.
- The [official supporting statement](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/DownloadDocument?objectID=145779901) anticipates a late-2026 summary report and publication of disclosure-protected microdata on the Board’s website.

**Why this rating:** the absence of a 2025 public dataset on October 9, 2026 does not itself establish delay: the announced release window is “late 2026.” That window applies explicitly to summary results; the supporting statement also promises public microdata but does not provide an equally precise separate microdata deadline.

**Confidence:** High for approval status and announced schedule; lower for actual completed fieldwork and forthcoming release readiness.

---

## 3. Data Quality

### Selected level: **Moderate Risk**

**This is a prospective capacity-risk rating, not a finding that published SCF data have already deteriorated.**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | Not supported; the collection continues. |
| **High Risk** | No implemented reduction in SCF frequency, public granularity, or announced publication timeliness was identified. |
| **Moderate Risk** | Staffing reductions, restricted hiring, and reduced technology investment create a plausible emerging risk to processing and publication capacity. |
| **No Known Issue** | Strong counterevidence: detailed public products remain available, the 2025 approval preserves the triennial design, and the last released wave improved some subgroup coverage. |

### Supporting evidence

- [Powell’s May 2025 staff message](https://www.federalreserve.gov/foia/files/powell-message-202505.pdf) announced an approximately **10% reduction in overall staffing over the next several years**.
- The implementation note in the [2025 Board budget](https://www.federalreserve.gov/foia/files/2025boardbudget.pdf) describes hiring-freeze alignment and says some technology-modernization initiatives would not proceed at their originally budgeted levels.
- The Board’s [May 2026 Office of Minority and Women Inclusion report](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/May-2026-Report-to-the-Congress-on-the-Office-of-Minority-and-Women-Inclusion.htm) says 2025 hiring was limited mostly to research assistants, interns, and mission-critical positions.
- Conversely, the 2025 collection approval retains detailed financial domains, wealthy-family oversampling, and triennial frequency.
- The [2022 SCF report](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/October-2023-Changes-in-US-Family-Finances-from-2019-to-2022.htm) documents expanded sampling for selected racial/ethnic groups, improving precision and enabling separate reporting for Asian families.

**Why this rating:** the SCF requires specialized editing, multiple imputation, weighting, disclosure review, and documentation. Reduced institutional capacity could affect those activities. However, **I did not establish that SCF personnel or its collection contract have been cut**, and there is no demonstrated quality loss.

A strictly observed-output interpretation could reasonably rate this **No Known Issue**. I select Moderate Risk because the rubric explicitly includes *potential or emerging* risks.

**Confidence:** Moderate-low; the capacity concern is documented institutionally, but its SCF-specific effect remains unverified.

---

## 4. Statutory Context

### Selected level: **High Risk**

**This rating concerns legal protection of the specific collection—not evidence of imminent cancellation.**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | Not applicable under the rubric. |
| **High Risk** | The cited statutes establish broad monetary-policy responsibilities rather than a specific SCF collection and publication requirement. This fits the rubric’s vague-authorization criterion. |
| **Moderate Risk** | Plausible alternative: the survey is an important input to federal policy implementation and has no fully equivalent substitute. However, I did not establish that implementation legally requires this particular survey. |
| **No Known Issue** | There are named statutory authorities and strong programmatic uses, but no identified statute specifies the SCF’s required contents, frequency, or public release. |

### Supporting evidence

The [SCF approval record](https://omb.report/icr/202408-7100-005) and official supporting statement cite:

- **12 U.S.C. § 225a**: monetary-policy objectives.
- **12 U.S.C. § 263**, including § 263(c): Federal Open Market Committee responsibilities.

Those provisions support collection of relevant economic information. They do not expressly say that the Board must conduct or publish the SCF.

Substantial programmatic use nevertheless provides practical protection:

- The [Distributional Financial Accounts](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/dataviz/dfa/index.html) use the SCF to distribute aggregate household wealth.
- [CBO’s family-wealth analysis](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/60807) relies primarily on SCF data.
- The Federal Register describes it as the only source of representative information on the structure of U.S. families’ finances.

Other surveys, including SHED, measure related household financial conditions, but the Board describes [SHED as complementing and augmenting the SCF](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2026-economic-well-being-of-us-households-in-2025-description.htm), not replacing it.

**Why this rating:** under the rubric’s literal “and/or” formulation, broad authority that does not specify the collection is sufficient for High Risk. Strong use and uniqueness mitigate practical risk, but are not equivalent to a survey-specific statutory mandate. Active OMB approval authorizes collection; it does not compel continued collection or publication.

**Confidence:** High on the absence of a requirement in the cited authorities; Moderate on classification because the rubric’s statutory categories overlap.

## 5. Staffing and Funding

### Selected level: **Moderate Risk**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | No evidence of elimination of the responsible unit or termination of SCF funding. |
| **High Risk** | No verified loss meeting the stated thresholds, ≥20% relevant budget cut, or effective forced removal of the threatened governors was established. |
| **Moderate Risk** | Threatened leadership removal meets an explicit rubric trigger. Announced staffing reductions and restricted hiring add concern. |
| **No Known Issue** | Not the best fit given documented leadership threats and workforce-reduction plans, although the approved SCF budget provides counterevidence. |

### Supporting evidence

**Risk indicators**

- Powell’s staff message announced about **10% overall staffing reduction** over several years.
- [Reuters reported the plan](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/us-federal-reserve-aims-trim-staff-by-10-coming-years-2025-05-16/) against a roughly 24,000-person System workforce.
- [October 1, 2026 reporting](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/01/trump-fed-powell-lisa-cook-michael-barr-removal.html) describes potential removal efforts involving Powell, Cook, and Barr.
- The [Supreme Court’s Cook decision](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/25a312_5468.pdf) concerns the attempted removal and continuation of litigation. An attempted removal should not be counted as an accomplished staff loss.

**Protective evidence**

- The 2025 Board budget allocated **$19.8 million to the triennial SCF**.
- The [2024 annual-report budget tables](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2024-ar-federal-reserve-system-budgets.htm) show a higher approved 2025 Board operating budget and a small increase in authorized Research and Statistics positions.
- Those are **budget authorizations**, not proof of actual spending or filled positions. The budget’s implementation note expressly warns that spending can be reduced without formal budget amendment.

**Staffing-tracker limitations**

I consulted the [USAJobs Listings Tracker](https://usajobs-tracker.abigailhaddad.com). It states that:

- Job listings are **not actual hires**.
- Not all federal positions appear on USAJobs.
- Collection was scheduled to stop December 31, 2025.

Consequently, it cannot establish 2026 SCF staffing losses or the rubric’s separation thresholds.

**Why this rating:** threatened leadership change independently supports Moderate Risk. A planned 10% System reduction is not proof that 10% of SCF staff—or 1,000 actual staff—have already departed.

**Confidence:** High for institutional threats; low for the magnitude of SCF-specific staffing or spending changes.

## 6. Policy

### Selected level: **No Known Issue**

**There are political warning signs, but no identified SCF-specific policy change.**

| Rubric level | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| **Gone** | No termination identified. |
| **High Risk** | No presidential-action-driven SCF ICR, negative SCF policy notice, or implemented administration-driven change to survey contents or publication was identified. |
| **Moderate Risk** | Broader administration-aligned institutional changes are relevant context, but I found no specific pending proposal or official statement to change the SCF. |
| **No Known Issue** | The collection continues under a pre-January-2025 approval, and the Board announced its continuation after January 2025. |

### Supporting evidence

- The operative ICR was approved in **August 2024**, without change; it is not identified as presidential-action-driven.
- The February 2025 announcement positively describes the SCF’s importance and commits to late-2026 results.
- [Reuters reported January 2025 removal of Federal Reserve diversity-related web content](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/fed-axed-diversity-section-website-around-time-trumps-executive-order-2025-01-23/), including workforce demographic information. This demonstrates that politically sensitive material at the same institution can be removed.
- However, those were **workforce/diversity resources, not SCF microdata**. I found no evidence linking that action to withdrawal of SCF race/ethnicity variables, subgroup tables, or financial-inequality research.
- Wealth inequality, racial wealth disparities, credit discrimination, and household vulnerability are politically salient SCF topics. Salience alone does not establish a proposed change.

**Why this rating:** the policy category asks about changes affecting what this dataset collects and publishes. Institutional political pressure is already reflected in Staffing and Funding; treating it as an implemented SCF policy change would overstate the evidence.

**Confidence:** Moderate; the 2025 public instrument and final microdata are not yet available for a complete cross-wave comparison.

---

## Preservation implications

The evidence supports **preventive preservation, not an emergency claim that the SCF is disappearing**.

Priorities are to:

1. Preserve all public waves, replicate weights, implicates, construction code, documentation, and dated change notes.
2. Retain release vintages separately; historical extracts can change through corrections and inflation rebasing.
3. Monitor the **late-2026 publication window** and **August 2027 approval expiration**.
4. Compare the forthcoming 2025 release against 2022 for missing variables, subgroup coverage, sample size, and documentation.
5. Seek actual SCF-unit staffing and expenditure evidence before interpreting System-wide plans as realized program cuts.
